why: LAB map. Tests the time slider on First World War fighting: the Western Front and Africa together, a month at a time, with the Western Front line moving through the war. Not a lesson map and not for MapMaker until the open checks in maps/data/ww1/SOURCES.md are settled.

item.title: LAB: First World War fighting, Western Front and Africa, 1914 to 1918 v0.5
item.snippet: Test map: move the time slider a month at a time to see where First World War fighting happened on the Western Front and across Africa, and where the Western Front ran. Draft.
item.description:
Test map. Where fighting happened in the First World War, month by month from August 1914 to November 1918, on the Western Front and across Africa: Togoland, Kamerun, German South West Africa, East and Central Africa, North Africa, and risings against colonial rule.

Time slider: it steps one month at a time, landing on the 11th of each month, and ends on 11 November 1918. Large coloured symbols show fighting during that month, each labelled with its name. Small grey dots show fighting in earlier months. A battle shows for every month it was fought in, so a battle at the end of a month appears from that month's first step.

Symbols: circles are battles, sieges and raids; squares are captures and surrenders; diamonds are risings against colonial rule. The legend names each, so colour is not the only clue.

Western Front: a dashed line shows how far the German armies got in September 1914. A solid line shows the front from late 1914 to March 1917, then after the German withdrawal to the Hindenburg Line from March 1917 to March 1918, then on dates from 10 June to 30 October 1918 (on this slider: June, July, August and September), then at 11 a.m. on 11 November 1918. Each line is labelled with its name. There is no line yet for April, May and October 1918, and some 1918 lines stop short of the sea or the Swiss border because their source maps do. The lines are good at Europe or region scale, usually within a few kilometres; each pop-up says what its line leaves out.

Where the points are: a battle fought over a wide area is shown at one place; the pop-up says where. Each pop-up names its source.

Sources: battle dates and facts from the National Army Museum, the American Battle Monuments Commission, The National Archives (UK), 1914-1918-online, London Gazette despatches and others named in each record. Front lines: The Western Theatre of the European War, 1918 edition (Société Editrice Géographique, Paris), Harry S. Truman Library & Museum, M1236, checked against Truman Library M549; Length of front occupied by Belgian, French, British and American forces, June to October 1918, G-3, GHQ, American Expeditionary Forces (Truman Library, M557 to M571); Order of Battle on Western Front, 11 A.M., Nov. 11, 1918, G-3, GHQ, American Expeditionary Forces (Library of Congress). Place positions: GeoNames.

Map version 0.5.0 (27 November 2026), lab draft.

basemap.title: Modern Antique
basemap.why: The same basemap as the other GIS for Schools maps. No reference label layer: countries are named from the data, so today's country names don't sit on the borders of 1914 to 1947.

symbol.why: Dark red and thick, so it reads on the antique basemap and against the coloured symbols. Dashed for the 1914 limit, which was never a held front, so line style as well as the legend tells the two apart.
